```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dpi = 150)
source(params$module_path)
dir.create(params$fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(params$table_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
# gene_map.tsv is regenerated in full from the normalized GTF by
# make_report_archive.sh each round — every tested gene has a symbol entry.
gene_map <- read_tsv(params$gene_map_path, col_types = "cccc", progress = FALSE)
sym <- function(ids) gene_map$symbol[match(ids, gene_map$gene_id)]
# display symbol: fall back to the gene ID when the GTF has no gene_name
symd <- function(ids) ifelse(is.na(sym(ids)) | sym(ids) == "", ids, sym(ids))
```

```{r load-data}
grouped   <- load_layer(params$data_dir, "grouped")
ungrouped <- load_layer(params$data_dir, "ungrouped")
combined  <- load_layer(params$data_dir, "combined") %>% driver_modality()
independent <- load_independent(params$data_dir)

# Sample sizes: infer per ancestry from the expression layer
# (n = ma_count / (2*af), median over genes). Modality layers differ by a
# few samples (modality-specific harmonization); the range is reported.
n_samp <- grouped %>% filter(modality == "expression") %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>%
  summarise(n = round(median(ma_count / (2 * af))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tibble::deframe()
n_samp <- n_samp[c("EAS", "EUR")]
n_range <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(ancestry, layer, modality) %>%
  summarise(n = round(median(ma_count / (2 * af))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>%
  summarise(n_min = min(n), n_max = max(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tibble::deframe()
```

# Executive summary

```{r exec-numbers}
fdr <- 0.05
n_cells <- nrow(bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
                  distinct(layer, ancestry, modality))
yield <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(layer, ancestry, modality) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), fdr05 = sum(qval <= fdr), fdr10 = sum(qval <= 0.10),
            min_q = min(qval), .groups = "drop")
n_fdr05 <- sum(yield$fdr05)

# FDR-significant hits per layer; the primary eGene catalog is the combined
# cross-modality layer, with per-modality grouped eGenes as the breakdown
# (ungrouped phenotype-level hits are descriptive only).
hits <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>% filter(qval <= fdr)
egenes_combined <- combined %>% filter(qval <= fdr)
egenes_grouped  <- grouped %>% filter(qval <= fdr)
n_eg <- egenes_combined %>% count(ancestry, name = "n") %>% tibble::deframe()
n_eg <- n_eg[c("EAS", "EUR")]; n_eg[is.na(n_eg)] <- 0L
n_eg_mod <- egenes_grouped %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "n")

# top association overall + per ancestry (for the headline)
top_hit <- bind_rows(grouped, combined, ungrouped) %>%
  slice_min(qval, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
top_by_anc <- bind_rows(grouped, combined, ungrouped) %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>% slice_min(qval, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
best_null <- if (any(yield$fdr05 == 0)) min(yield$min_q[yield$fdr05 == 0]) else NA_real_

# carrier-count audit (MAC >= 5 floor baked into the genotype intersection
# at module 23 this round — verify it propagated to the mapping outputs)
mac_audit <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>%
  summarise(min_carriers = min(ma_count), n_lt5 = sum(ma_count < 5),
            .groups = "drop")

# short inline helpers for data-driven prose
fmt_genes <- function(ids) paste0("_", symd(ids), "_", collapse = ", ")
describe_hit <- function(h) {
  sprintf("%s (%s, %s layer, q = %s)", symd(h$gene_id), h$modality, h$layer,
          signif(h$qval, 2))
}
```

This report summarizes the multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis:
cohort-only genotype PCA on LD-pruned variants within each ancestry stratum,
a conventional covariate set (first 5 genotype PCs + HCP factors + sex,
gestational age, and cell-type fractions; maternal cell fraction excluded
before correlation pruning at |r| > 0.9; HCP count optimized per ancestry
via module 25a; no covariate cap), a MAF ≥ 0.01 filter with a ≥ 5
minor-allele-count floor at the
genotype intersection, Storey q-values (computed with the R `qvalue`
package), and per-phenotype rank-based inverse-normal transformation of all
modalities (isoform usage mapped as within-gene relative-abundance ratios;
isoform expression as transcript-level TPM abundance).
Mapping covers
`r n_cells` ancestry × modality × layer cells (EAS n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`,
EUR n ≈ `r n_samp["EUR"]`).

```{r exec-pi1}
pi1_cells <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(layer, ancestry, modality) %>%
  summarise(pi1 = storey_pi1(pval_beta), .groups = "drop")
pi1_range <- range(pi1_cells$pi1, na.rm = TRUE)
hit_r2 <- if (nrow(hits) > 0) range(approx_r2(hits$slope, hits$af)) else NULL
```

**Headline result: `r n_fdr05` association`r if (n_fdr05 != 1) "s"` reach`r if (n_fdr05 == 1) "es"` FDR ≤ 5%**
across the `r n_cells` ancestry × modality × layer cells. The primary eGene
catalog (combined cross-modality layer) contains **`r n_eg["EAS"]` EAS and
`r n_eg["EUR"]` EUR eGenes** at FDR ≤ 5%; per-modality grouped eGenes are
the breakdown, and ungrouped phenotype-level hits are reported descriptively
(Results). Strongest association per ancestry:
`r paste(sprintf("%s: %s", top_by_anc$ancestry, apply(top_by_anc, 1, function(r) sprintf("%s (%s, %s layer, q = %s)", symd(r[["gene_id"]]), r[["modality"]], r[["layer"]], signif(as.numeric(r[["qval"]]), 2)))), collapse = "; ")`.
`r if (!is.na(best_null)) sprintf("Outside the FDR-significant set, the best remaining q-value anywhere is %s.", signif(best_null, 2))`
Storey calibration estimates a signal fraction (π1) of
`r round(100 * pi1_range[1])`–`r round(100 * pi1_range[2])`% across cells;
at these fractions Storey q-values are numerically close to
Benjamini–Hochberg (Diagnostics).

For the cells without FDR discoveries, three lines of evidence indicate the
residual null is a **power limitation, not a pipeline failure**:

1. **Calibration is healthy** — permutation-calibrated p-values track the
   null through the bulk in every layer (QQ plots, Diagnostics), and a
   low π1 is the expected outcome when true effects are mostly below the
   detection floor.
2. **Detectable effect sizes remain large at our n** — minimum detectable
   effect (80% power) is r² ≈ 0.10 at n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]` (EAS) and
   r² ≈ 0.19 at n ≈ `r n_samp["EUR"]` (EUR), versus ≈ 0.06 at
   PANTRY/Geuvadis n = 445. Typical cis-xQTLs explain 5–15% of phenotype
   variance — mostly below our floor.
   `r if (!is.null(hit_r2)) sprintf("The FDR-significant hits carry estimated r² of %.2f–%.2f — exactly the class of outsize effect the floor permits.", hit_r2[1], hit_r2[2])`
3. **Sub-threshold tails are not shared between ancestries** — cross-ancestry
   rank concordance of gene-level signal is ≈ 0, as expected if near-misses
   are noise rather than shared weak signal.

`r if (all(mac_audit$n_lt5 == 0)) sprintf("**Carrier-count audit: clean.** The MAC ≥ 5 floor (applied at the genotype intersection in module 23) propagated to every mapping output — minimum minor-allele carrier count across all tested pairs is %d (EAS) and %d (EUR).", mac_audit$min_carriers[mac_audit$ancestry == "EAS"], mac_audit$min_carriers[mac_audit$ancestry == "EUR"]) else sprintf("**Carrier-count caveat.** A fraction of tested pairs retain < 5 minor-allele carriers in the mapping sample sets (EAS: %d tests; EUR: %d tests; audit table below) — the MAC ≥ 5 floor was applied before outlier exclusion. Flagged tests should be discounted; no FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited.", mac_audit$n_lt5[mac_audit$ancestry == "EAS"], mac_audit$n_lt5[mac_audit$ancestry == "EUR"])`

# Data and methods

## Pipeline recap

- **Phenotypes**: 9 RNA modalities (gene expression, isoform usage, isoform
  expression, splice junction usage, intron retention, alternative TSS,
  alternative polyA, RNA editing, RNA stability), harmonized to genotyped
  samples (array_id), with NIGMS technical replicates averaged per
  individual. The two isoform modalities are both built from QU-corrected
  Salmon transcript counts (mean count ≥ 10): **isoform usage** is
  within-gene relative-abundance ratios (transcript TPM / gene-total TPM;
  PANTRY convention, mean ratio in [0.05, 0.95]) and **isoform expression**
  is the pre-ratio transcript TPM abundance (devBrain §3.3 convention).
  Per ancestry stratum:
  feature filtering (isoform usage: usage > 0.1 in > 25% of samples;
  isoform expression: TPM > 0.1 in > 25% of samples, devBrain
  §3.3; ratio modalities: detected in ≥ 40%, devBrain §3.4),
  batch-median NA imputation, quantile normalization across samples +
  rank-based inverse-normal transformation per phenotype, then ComBat
  (batch = cohort) **last** — the devBrain "ComBat on the normalized data"
  convention. No log2 pre-transform is applied: rank-based INT is invariant
  to any monotone transform, so log2/VST would be exact no-ops on the
  mapped scale.
- **Genotypes**: ancestry-stratified plink2 pgen; variants filtered to
  **MAF ≥ 0.01 with MAC ≥ 5** (≥ 5 minor alleles) at the genotype
  intersection — the count floor excludes low-carrier tests, which can
  produce spurious associations, while MAF 0.01 keeps the variant pool as
  large as defensible. tensorQTL's own MAF ≥ 0.01 filter applies on top at
  mapping time.
- **Genotype PCA**: cohort-only PCA per ancestry on LD-pruned variants
  (plink2 `--indep-pairwise 200 50 0.2`, then `--pca 20 exact`) — the GTEx
  convention.
- **Covariates**: per ancestry, first-5 genotype PCs + HCP factors 1–k\*
  (k\* selected by module 25a, chr1 eGene maximization) + sex + gestational
  age + cell-type fractions (Syncytiotrophoblast as reference). The maternal
  cell-fraction covariate (`ct_Maternal`) is excluded BEFORE pruning by
  analysis decision (coded `--exclude-covariates`, replacing the round-3
  hand-edit); the remaining pool is correlation-pruned (iterative max-|r| >
  0.9 removal, protecting sex/GA > PCs > cell types > HCPs — correlated
  HCPs are dropped, so effective k can fall below nominal k\*) with **no
  covariate cap** (details and QC below).
- **Mapping** (tensorQTL, cis window ±1 Mb): (i) **per-modality grouped** —
  all phenotypes of a gene within a modality tested as one group
  (permutation-calibrated gene-level p-value; the row label is the
  *driver phenotype*); (ii) **combined** — all phenotypes of a gene across
  all modalities as one cross-modality group (PANTRY's headline design);
  (iii) **ungrouped** — per-phenotype lead variants for transcript-level
  resolution; (iv) **stepwise** (`cis.map_independent`) for conditionally
  independent signals, entered at FDR ≤ 5%.
- **Multiple testing**: **Storey q-values** on the
  permutation-calibrated p-value (pval_beta), computed with the R `qvalue`
  package (default lambda) — the GTEx convention, and statistically
  identical to tensorQTL's own `calculate_qvalues`. (On this cluster the
  rpy2/conda-R route to `qvalue` hits an unresolvable libstdc++/GLIBCXX
  conflict, so q-values are computed through a file-based bridge to the
  singularity R container used elsewhere in the pipeline.)

## Genotype PCA and covariate QC

```{r covariate-qc}
qc_in <- file.path(params$qc_dir, "qtl_inputs")
qc_pc <- file.path(params$qc_dir, "genotype_pcs")
cov_sets <- lapply(c("EAS", "EUR"), function(a) {
  read_tsv(file.path(qc_in, paste0(a, "_covariates.tsv")),
           col_types = cols(.default = col_double(), covariate_id = col_character()),
           progress = FALSE)
})
names(cov_sets) <- c("EAS", "EUR")
cov_summary <- tibble(
  ancestry = c("EAS", "EUR"),
  n_covariates = sapply(cov_sets, nrow),
  n_samples    = sapply(cov_sets, ncol) - 1L,
  genotype_PCs = sapply(cov_sets, function(d)
    paste(d$covariate_id[grepl("^PC", d$covariate_id)], collapse = ", ")),
  n_HCP        = sapply(cov_sets, function(d) sum(grepl("^HCP", d$covariate_id))),
  n_celltypes  = sapply(cov_sets, function(d) sum(grepl("^ct_", d$covariate_id))))
knitr::kable(cov_summary,
             caption = "Final covariate sets (as mapped). Maternal cell-fraction covariate excluded before pruning by analysis decision; HCP count per ancestry from module 25a; no covariate cap.")
write_tsv(cov_summary, file.path(params$table_dir, "covariate_summary.tsv"))

prune <- bind_rows(lapply(c("EAS", "EUR"), function(a)
  read_tsv(file.path(qc_in, paste0(a, "_covariate_pruning.tsv")),
           col_types = "cccc", progress = FALSE) %>% mutate(ancestry = a)))
knitr::kable(prune %>% select(ancestry, everything()),
             caption = "Covariate pruning log: analysis-decision exclusions, reference cell type, and correlation pruning (|r| > 0.9; HCPs lowest priority — no covariate cap).")
write_tsv(prune, file.path(params$table_dir, "covariate_pruning.tsv"))

prune_by_reason <- prune %>% count(ancestry, reason) %>%
  mutate(reason = factor(reason, levels = c("excluded", "reference_cell_type",
                                            "zero_variance", "correlated",
                                            "cap_25"))) %>%
  arrange(ancestry, reason)
prune_fmt <- function(a) paste(sprintf("%s %s", prune_by_reason$n[prune_by_reason$ancestry == a],
                                       prune_by_reason$reason[prune_by_reason$ancestry == a]),
                               collapse = ", ")
pcs_retained <- sapply(cov_sets, function(d)
  all(paste0("PC", 1:5) %in% d$covariate_id))

outl <- bind_rows(lapply(c("EAS", "EUR"), function(a)
  read_tsv(file.path(qc_in, paste0(a, "_outliers.tsv")),
           col_types = "ccnnnn", progress = FALSE) %>% mutate(ancestry = a)))
n_outl <- outl %>% distinct(ancestry, sample_id) %>% count(ancestry, name = "samples_removed")
knitr::kable(outl %>% select(ancestry, sample_id, pc, sd_distance) %>%
               arrange(ancestry, desc(sd_distance)), digits = 2,
             caption = "PCA outliers excluded (6-SD rule on PC1–PC5, cohort-only PCA).")
```

Outlier exclusion on the cohort-only PCs (6-SD rule on PC1–PC5) removed
`r n_outl$samples_removed[n_outl$ancestry == "EAS"]` EAS and
`r n_outl$samples_removed[n_outl$ancestry == "EUR"]` EUR samples. Pruning
dropped `r sum(prune_by_reason$n[prune_by_reason$ancestry == "EAS"])`
covariates in EAS (`r prune_fmt("EAS")`) and
`r sum(prune_by_reason$n[prune_by_reason$ancestry == "EUR"])` in EUR
(`r prune_fmt("EUR")`); both ancestries retained all of PC1–PC5:
`r pcs_retained`. Correlated-HCP drops (if any) reduce effective k below the
nominal 25a optimum — see the HCP-optimization section.

```{r scree-eas, fig.width=7, fig.height=4, out.width="49%", eval=file.exists(file.path(qc_pc, "EAS_genotype_pcs_scree.png"))}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(qc_pc, "EAS_genotype_pcs_scree.png"))
```

```{r scree-eur, fig.width=7, fig.height=4, out.width="49%", eval=file.exists(file.path(qc_pc, "EUR_genotype_pcs_scree.png"))}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(qc_pc, "EUR_genotype_pcs_scree.png"))
```

Scree plots (cohort-only PCA, LD-pruned variants): PC1 carries ≈ 13–14% of
pruned-variant variance in both strata, with a smooth, shallow decay
thereafter (PC2 ≈ 6–9%) and no sharp elbow — the expected spectrum within
ancestry-stratified subsets, and the basis for the first-5-PCs rule.

```{r covcor-figs, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, out.width="49%", fig.show="hold"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(qc_in, "EAS_covariate_correlation.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(qc_in, "EUR_covariate_correlation.png"))
```

Covariate correlation matrices before/after pruning: no |r| > 0.9 pairs
remain in the final sets.

## HCP count optimization (module 25a)

```{r hcp-optimization, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
hcp_opt <- bind_rows(lapply(c("EAS", "EUR"), function(a) {
  f <- file.path(params$qc_dir, "hcp_optimization", paste0(a, "_optimal_hcp.tsv"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  read_tsv(f, col_types = cols(.default = col_double(), chosen = col_logical()),
           progress = FALSE) %>% mutate(ancestry = a)
}))
if (nrow(hcp_opt) > 0) {
  k_star <- hcp_opt %>% filter(chosen) %>% select(ancestry, k, n_egenes)
  p_hcp <- ggplot(hcp_opt, aes(k, n_egenes)) +
    geom_line(color = "#0279EE") +
    geom_point(aes(size = chosen), color = "#0279EE") +
    geom_point(data = hcp_opt %>% filter(chosen), color = "#D62728", size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = hcp_opt %>% filter(n_hcp_dropped > 0),
              aes(label = sprintf("eff. k=%d", n_hcp_used)),
              vjust = -0.9, size = 3, color = "grey30") +
    facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
    scale_size_manual(values = c(1.5, 3), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = "HCP factors (k)", y = "chr1 eGenes (Storey q ≤ 0.05)",
         caption = "Red: chosen k* (max eGenes, ties to smaller k). 'eff. k' annotates models where correlation pruning dropped HCPs.") +
    theme_report()
  print(p_hcp)
  ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_hcp_optimization.png"), p_hcp,
         width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
  knitr::kable(hcp_opt %>% select(ancestry, k, n_egenes, n_tested,
                                  n_hcp_used, n_hcp_dropped, chosen),
               caption = "25a grid: chr1 eGene yield per candidate HCP count (expression layer). n_hcp_used/dropped record correlation-pruning losses; chosen = k*.")
  write_tsv(hcp_opt, file.path(params$table_dir, "hcp_optimization.tsv"))
} else {
  cat("25a optimization output not found in the archive — section skipped.\n")
}
```

`r if (exists("hcp_opt") && nrow(hcp_opt) > 0) sprintf("Module 25a re-estimates HCPs at each candidate k on the pruned fixed covariate set (no cap), maps the chr1 expression layer per k, and selects k* by eGene yield: EAS k* = %d (%d eGenes), EUR k* = %d (%d eGenes). The k* solution is installed as the canonical harmonized HCP file for module 25.", k_star$k[k_star$ancestry == "EAS"], k_star$n_egenes[k_star$ancestry == "EAS"], k_star$k[k_star$ancestry == "EUR"], k_star$n_egenes[k_star$ancestry == "EUR"])`

## Test counts

```{r test-counts}
counts <- bind_rows(
  grouped %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "genes_tested"),
  combined %>% count(ancestry, name = "genes_tested") %>% mutate(modality = "combined")
) %>% arrange(ancestry, modality)
knitr::kable(counts, caption = "Genes tested per ancestry × modality (grouped layers).")
write_tsv(counts, file.path(params$table_dir, "test_counts.tsv"))
```

Note the ancestry asymmetry: EUR contributes roughly 1.3–5.6× more phenotypes
than EAS in the ungrouped layer (ancestry-specific phenotype filtering;
1.3× for splicing up to 5.6× for RNA editing),
while the gene universes are similar (~12–13k genes). Mapping sample sizes
vary slightly by modality (EAS `r n_range["EAS"]`, EUR `r n_range["EUR"]`
across layers, inferred from allele-count/frequency denominators) because
each modality's phenotype matrix harmonizes to a slightly different sample
set.

# PANTRY-style summary figures

## Phenotypes and genes per modality (PANTRY Fig 1b/c style)

```{r fig-phenotypes-genes, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
pheno_counts <- ungrouped %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "n_phenotypes")
expr_counts <- grouped %>% filter(modality == "expression") %>%
  count(ancestry, modality, name = "n_phenotypes")
pheno_counts <- bind_rows(pheno_counts, expr_counts)
gene_counts <- grouped %>% count(ancestry, modality, name = "n_genes")

p1a <- ggplot(pheno_counts, aes(modality, n_phenotypes, fill = modality)) +
  geom_col() + facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = MODALITY_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "phenotypes tested") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
p1b <- ggplot(gene_counts, aes(modality, n_genes, fill = modality)) +
  geom_col() + facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = MODALITY_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "genes tested") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
p1 <- p1a + p1b + patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
print(p1)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig1_phenotypes_genes_per_modality.png"), p1,
       width = 10, height = 4.6, dpi = 150)
```

## xGenes per modality — q-value tiers (PANTRY Fig 2a adapted)

At FDR ≤ 5% the grouped (gene-level, per-modality) layers contain
**`r nrow(egenes_grouped)` ancestry × modality × gene hits**`r if (nrow(n_eg_mod) > 0) sprintf(" (%s)", paste(sprintf("%s %s: %d", n_eg_mod$ancestry, n_eg_mod$modality, n_eg_mod$n), collapse = ", "))`;
the combined cross-modality layer adds `r sum(n_eg)` eGenes. The figure
shows the full q-value landscape: genes binned by best q-value per
ancestry × modality.

```{r fig-xgenes-tiers, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
tiers <- grouped %>%
  mutate(tier = cut(qval, breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 1),
                    labels = c("q≤0.05", "q≤0.10", "q≤0.25", "q≤0.50", "q>0.50"),
                    include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  count(ancestry, modality, tier, .drop = FALSE)
tier_cols <- c("q≤0.05" = "#D62728", "q≤0.10" = "#FF9400", "q≤0.25" = "#E9ED4C",
               "q≤0.50" = "#9ECAE1", "q>0.50" = "grey85")
near_miss <- tiers %>% filter(tier %in% c("q≤0.05", "q≤0.10", "q≤0.25")) %>%
  group_by(ancestry, tier) %>% summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n > 0)
near_miss_label <- if (nrow(near_miss) == 0) "no genes at q ≤ 0.25" else
  paste(sprintf("%s: %d gene(s) at %s", near_miss$ancestry, near_miss$n, near_miss$tier),
        collapse = "; ")
p2 <- ggplot(tiers, aes(modality, n, fill = factor(tier, levels = names(tier_cols)))) +
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tier_cols, name = "best q-value\nper gene") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "genes",
       caption = paste0("Near-miss genes: ", near_miss_label, ".")) +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
print(p2)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig2a_xgenes_qvalue_tiers.png"), p2,
       width = 10, height = 5.2, dpi = 150)
```

## Phenotypes per gene group (PANTRY Fig 2b adapted)

```{r stepwise-stats}
# conditionally independent signals per group (rank 1 = primary lead)
indep_summary <- if (nrow(independent) > 0 && "rank" %in% names(independent)) {
  independent %>%
    group_by(ancestry, modality, group_id = phenotype_id) %>%
    summarise(n_signals = max(rank), .groups = "drop")
} else {
  tibble(ancestry = character(), modality = character(),
         group_id = character(), n_signals = integer())
}
n_groups_stepwise <- nrow(indep_summary)
n_secondary <- sum(indep_summary$n_signals > 1)
```

`r if (n_groups_stepwise == 0) "No group entered the stepwise scan this round (no FDR ≤ 5% entrant in any ancestry × modality layer), so no conditionally independent signals were called." else sprintf("Stepwise regression (cis.map_independent) ran on %d FDR-qualifying groups; %d group(s) carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (rank ≥ 2).", n_groups_stepwise, n_secondary)`
The design-level view below shows how many phenotypes each gene contributes
to its group (the multiple-testing unit).

```{r fig-group-size, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
gs <- bind_rows(
  grouped %>% filter(modality != "expression") %>%
    select(ancestry, modality, group_size),
  combined %>% select(ancestry, modality, group_size)
)
p3 <- ggplot(gs, aes(modality, group_size, fill = modality)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(MODALITY_COLORS, combined = "#ECE9E2"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "phenotypes per gene group (log10)") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
print(p3)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig2b_phenotypes_per_group.png"), p3,
       width = 10, height = 4.4, dpi = 150)
```

Combined groups integrate a median of ~4–5 phenotypes per gene (max > 100) —
the cross-modality burden-sharing the PANTRY design exploits. (Stability
shows a flat box at 1 by design: one phenotype per gene.)

## Driver-variant position relative to the gene body (PANTRY Fig 2d style)

```{r fig-variant-position, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
# regenerated from the normalized GTF by make_report_archive.sh:
# gene_id, chr, start, end, strand (±1)
gene_bodies <- read_tsv(params$gene_bodies_path, col_types = "cciii",
                        progress = FALSE)
top200 <- bind_rows(
  grouped %>% filter(modality != "expression") %>%
    group_by(ancestry, modality) %>% slice_min(pval_beta, n = 200, with_ties = FALSE),
  combined %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% slice_min(pval_beta, n = 200, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(modality = factor("combined", levels = c(MODALITY_LEVELS, "combined")))
) %>% ungroup() %>% add_gene_relative_position(gene_bodies) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rel_pos), abs(rel_pos - 0.5) <= 1.5)

p4 <- ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = top200 %>% filter(modality != "combined"),
               aes(rel_pos, fill = modality), alpha = 0.55, color = NA, adjust = 1.2) +
  geom_density(data = top200 %>% filter(modality == "combined"),
               aes(rel_pos), color = "#333333", linewidth = 1.1, linetype = 2,
               fill = NA, adjust = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = MODALITY_COLORS, name = NULL) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0, 1), linetype = 2, color = "grey40") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.6, 1.6)) +
  labs(x = "driver-variant position relative to gene body (0 = 5' end, 1 = 3' end)",
       y = "density (top 200 genes per layer)",
       caption = "Dashed line: combined cross-modality layer.") +
  theme_report()
print(p4)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig2d_variant_position_top200.png"), p4,
       width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

`r if (n_fdr05 <= 10) "With few FDR-significant associations, these densities describe essentially the sub-threshold tail; any positional enrichment should be read as descriptive." else "Densities are computed over the top 200 genes per layer (FDR-significant plus sub-threshold); read as a positional summary of the strongest signals."`

## Expression vs non-expression near-miss genes (PANTRY Supp Fig 2 adapted)

```{r expr-vs-nonexpr}
expr_best <- grouped %>% filter(modality == "expression") %>%
  select(ancestry, gene_id, expr_q = qval)
nonexpr_best <- grouped %>% filter(modality != "expression") %>%
  group_by(ancestry, gene_id) %>% slice_min(qval, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  summarise(best_nonexpr_q = min(qval), .groups = "drop")
cmp <- expr_best %>% inner_join(nonexpr_best, by = c("ancestry", "gene_id"))
n_nonexpr_better <- cmp %>% group_by(ancestry) %>%
  summarise(frac_nonexpr_better = mean(best_nonexpr_q < expr_q),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(n_nonexpr_better, digits = 3,
             caption = "Fraction of genes whose best non-expression xQTL q-value beats their expression q-value (tested in both).")
write_tsv(n_nonexpr_better, file.path(params$table_dir, "expr_vs_nonexpr.tsv"))
```

A majority of genes have a non-expression modality as their best (lowest)
q-value — expected, since non-expression modalities test each gene against
multiple phenotypes. `r if (nrow(egenes_grouped) <= 1) "With at most one gene-level FDR hit this remains a descriptive pattern, not evidence of non-expression-specific regulation." else "The FDR-significant eGene breakdown by modality (Results) shows whether this tail pattern converts into discoveries."`

# Calibration and diagnostics

## Permutation-calibrated p-value QQ plots

```{r fig-qq, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
qq <- bind_rows(
  combined %>% select(ancestry, modality, pval_beta),
  grouped %>% select(ancestry, modality, pval_beta)
) %>% group_by(ancestry, modality) %>%
  group_modify(~ qq_data(.x$pval_beta)) %>% ungroup()
# thin the null bulk for plotting; keep the full tail (observed > 3)
qq_plot <- qq %>% group_by(ancestry, modality) %>%
  filter(observed >= 3 | dplyr::row_number() %% 25 == 0) %>% ungroup()

p5 <- ggplot(qq_plot, aes(expected, observed, color = modality)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~ancestry) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(MODALITY_COLORS, combined = "#D62728"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "expected -log10(pval_beta)", y = "observed -log10(pval_beta)") +
  theme_report()
print(p5)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_qq_pval_beta.png"), p5,
       width = 10, height = 5.2, dpi = 150)
```

Calibrated p-values track the null through the bulk with at most a modest
short tail — the signature of few-or-no detectable associations, without
systematic inflation (which would bend the whole curve up) or deflation.

## Signal fraction (Storey π1) per layer

```{r pi1-table}
pi1_tab <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(layer, ancestry, modality) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pi1 = storey_pi1(pval_beta), min_q = min(qval),
            .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(layer, ancestry, desc(pi1))
knitr::kable(pi1_tab, digits = 3,
             caption = "Storey pi1 (estimated fraction of true associations) on permutation-calibrated p-values.")
write_tsv(pi1_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "pi1_summary.tsv"))

# Verify the pipeline's Storey q-values: with pi0 near 1 they nearly reduce
# to BH on pval_beta. Report the max |q - BH| per ancestry (combined layer).
bh_check <- combined %>% group_by(ancestry) %>%
  summarise(max_abs_q_minus_BH = max(abs(qval - p.adjust(pval_beta, method = "BH"))),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r pi1-text}
pi1_range <- range(pi1_tab$pi1, na.rm = TRUE)
```

π1 estimates are `r round(100*pi1_range[1])`–`r round(100*pi1_range[2])`%
across all cells`r if (pi1_range[2] <= 0.05) " — at most a trace signal fraction, concentrated in the highest-signal layers" else sprintf(", with the largest fractions in %s", paste(pi1_tab %>% slice_max(pi1, n = 2) %>% mutate(lbl = paste(ancestry, modality, layer)) %>% pull(lbl), collapse = " and "))`. Storey q-values remain close to BH on this
data (max |q − BH| across the combined layer =
`r signif(max(bh_check$max_abs_q_minus_BH), 2)`). Storey remains the correct
convention — it can only help as signal grows (π0 < 1) — but it provides
little lift at low signal fractions.

## Power analysis

```{r fig-power, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ns <- seq(50, 500, by = 5)
alpha_expr <- 0.05 / (grouped %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS", modality == "expression") %>% nrow())
pow_curve <- tibble(n = ns,
                    r2 = sapply(ns, min_detectable_r2, alpha = alpha_expr, power = 0.8))
p6 <- ggplot(pow_curve, aes(n, r2)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(n_samp["EAS"], n_samp["EUR"], 445),
             linetype = c(2, 2, 3), color = c("#0279EE", "#FF9400", "grey40")) +
  annotate("text", x = n_samp["EAS"], y = 0.87, hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5,
           label = sprintf("EAS (n≈%d)", n_samp["EAS"])) +
  annotate("text", x = n_samp["EUR"], y = 0.80, hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5,
           label = sprintf("EUR (n≈%d)", n_samp["EUR"])) +
  annotate("text", x = 445, y = 0.73, label = "PANTRY/Geuvadis (n=445)", hjust = 1.05, size = 3.5) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 50, xmax = 500, ymin = 0.05, ymax = 0.15,
           alpha = 0.15, fill = "#75A025") +
  annotate("text", x = 490, y = 0.10, label = "typical cis-xQTL effect range", hjust = 1, size = 3.5) +
  labs(x = "sample size", y = "minimum detectable r² (80% power)") +
  theme_report()
print(p6)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_power_curve.png"), p6,
       width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r power-table}
power_tab <- bind_rows(
  grouped %>% group_by(ancestry, modality) %>% summarise(n_tested = n(), .groups = "drop"),
  combined %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% summarise(modality = "combined", n_tested = n(), .groups = "drop")
) %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(alpha = 0.05 / n_tested,
         n = n_samp[as.character(ancestry)],
         min_r2_our_n = min_detectable_r2(n, alpha),
         min_r2_pantry_n = min_detectable_r2(445, alpha)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% select(-n)
knitr::kable(power_tab, digits = 3,
             caption = "Minimum detectable effect (r², 80% power) at our sample sizes vs PANTRY's n=445, per layer.")
write_tsv(power_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "power_analysis.tsv"))
```

At n ≈ `r n_samp["EUR"]` (EUR), only xQTLs explaining ≳ 19% of phenotype
variance are detectable at genome-wide thresholds; the larger EAS stratum
(n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`) brings the floor to ≈ 10% — versus ≈ 6% at PANTRY's
n = 445. For reference, PANTRY (n = 445) reported 6,798 eGenes and a 66%
discovery gain from non-expression modalities; GTEx tissues at n ≈ 150
typically report hundreds to ~2,000 eGenes. Our yield this round
(`r n_fdr05` FDR ≤ 5% associations; `r sum(n_eg)` combined-layer eGenes)
sits `r if (sum(n_eg) < 100) "at the pessimistic end of" else "within"` that
range.

# Results

## FDR-significant associations

```{r hit-table}
hit_tab <- hits %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = symd(gene_id),
         modality_display = if_else(layer == "combined",
                                    paste0("combined (driver: ", driver_modality, ")"),
                                    as.character(modality)),
         target = str_split_fixed(original_id, "__", 2)[, 2],
         # distance to the target itself: parse the coordinate when the
         # phenotype id encodes one (e.g. RNA-editing sites); otherwise use
         # tensorQTL's start_distance (distance to the phenotype TSS)
         target_pos = suppressWarnings(
           as.numeric(str_match(target, "^chr[0-9XYM]+_(\\d+)$")[, 2])),
         variant_to_target_kb = round(abs(if_else(!is.na(target_pos),
                                                  variant_pos - target_pos,
                                                  start_distance)) / 1000)) %>%
  arrange(ancestry, layer, qval) %>%
  select(ancestry, layer, modality_display, gene_id, gene_symbol, phenotype_id,
         target, variant_id, af, ma_count, slope, pval_nominal, pval_beta,
         qval, variant_to_target_kb)
knitr::kable(hit_tab %>% slice_head(n = 100), digits = 3,
             caption = sprintf("FDR ≤ 5%% associations across layers (top 100 of %d shown; full table in tables/fdr_hits.tsv). Grouped/combined rows are gene-level; ungrouped rows are phenotype-level.", nrow(hit_tab)))
write_tsv(hit_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "fdr_hits.tsv"))
```

`r if (nrow(hit_tab) == 0) "No association reaches FDR ≤ 5% this round — the near-miss landscape below is the prioritization view."`

Per-gene context tables show each FDR-significant gene across all layers and
both ancestries (grouped/combined rows are gene-level; ungrouped rows are
phenotype-level leads). Read the pattern per gene: a hit confined to one
layer and one ancestry is ancestry- and modality-specific; a hit that also
passes in the combined layer survives the cross-modality grouping burden.

```{r hit-context, results='asis'}
hit_genes <- hits %>% distinct(ancestry, gene_id) %>% arrange(ancestry, gene_id)
max_context <- 12
ctx_genes <- hit_genes %>% slice_head(n = max_context)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ctx_genes))) {
  g <- ctx_genes$gene_id[i]
  a <- as.character(ctx_genes$ancestry[i])
  ctx <- bind_rows(
    grouped %>% filter(gene_id == g) %>%
      select(ancestry, modality, layer, variant_id, af, ma_count, pval_beta, qval),
    combined %>% filter(gene_id == g) %>%
      select(ancestry, modality = driver_modality, layer, variant_id, af,
             ma_count, pval_beta, qval),
    ungrouped %>% filter(gene_id == g) %>%
      select(ancestry, modality, layer, variant_id, af, ma_count, pval_beta, qval)
  ) %>% arrange(ancestry, qval)
  cat(sprintf("\n\n#### %s — %s\n\n", a, symd(g)))
  print(knitr::kable(ctx, digits = 3,
                     caption = sprintf("%s (%s) across layers and ancestries.",
                                       symd(g), g)))
}
if (nrow(hit_genes) > max_context) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n*%d further hit genes omitted from per-gene context tables; see tables/fdr_hits.tsv.*\n",
              nrow(hit_genes) - max_context))
}
```

All hits clear the MAC ≥ 5 carrier floor (audit below); visual QC of
phenotype levels by genotype and replication in larger placental cohorts
remain the required next steps before functional claims.

## Near-miss landscape

```{r near-miss-table}
near <- bind_rows(
  grouped %>% select(ancestry, modality, layer, gene_id, phenotype_id,
                     variant_id, af, ma_count, slope, pval_beta, qval),
  combined %>% select(ancestry, modality = driver_modality, layer, gene_id,
                      phenotype_id, variant_id, af, ma_count, slope,
                      pval_beta, qval),
  ungrouped %>% select(ancestry, modality, layer, gene_id, phenotype_id,
                       variant_id, af, ma_count, slope, pval_beta, qval)
) %>% filter(qval <= 0.25) %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = symd(gene_id),
         carrier_flag = if_else(ma_count < 5, "LOW CARRIER COUNT", "")) %>%
  arrange(qval) %>%
  select(ancestry, layer, modality, gene_id, gene_symbol, variant_id, af,
         ma_count, carrier_flag, slope, pval_beta, qval)
knitr::kable(near %>% slice_head(n = 100), digits = 3,
             caption = sprintf("Associations at q ≤ 0.25 across every layer (top 100 of %d shown; full table in tables/near_miss.tsv). Rows flagged LOW CARRIER COUNT have < 5 minor-allele carriers in the mapping sample set and should be discounted (see audit).", nrow(near)))
write_tsv(near, file.path(params$table_dir, "near_miss.tsv"))

near_nonhits <- near %>% filter(qval > 0.05) %>% slice_head(n = 3)
near_nonhits_txt <- paste(
  sprintf("%s (%s %s, %s layer, q = %s, %d carriers)", near_nonhits$gene_symbol,
          near_nonhits$ancestry, near_nonhits$modality, near_nonhits$layer,
          signif(near_nonhits$qval, 2), near_nonhits$ma_count),
  collapse = "; ")
n_low_carrier <- sum(near$carrier_flag != "")
```

The q ≤ 0.25 tail contains `r nrow(near)` rows (including the
`r nrow(hit_tab)` FDR-significant associations).
`r if (nrow(near_nonhits) > 0) paste0("The strongest non-hit associations: ", near_nonhits_txt, ".")`
`r if (n_low_carrier > 0) sprintf("%d row(s) retain < 5 minor-allele carriers (flagged); those should be discounted.", n_low_carrier) else "No row is carrier-limited (all ≥ 5 minor-allele carriers)."`

## Carrier-count audit: MAC floor propagation

```{r carrier-check}
mac_tab <- bind_rows(grouped, ungrouped, combined) %>%
  group_by(ancestry, layer) %>%
  summarise(min_carriers = min(ma_count), n_lt5 = sum(ma_count < 5),
            n_total = n(), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(mac_tab,
             caption = "Minimum minor-allele carrier counts per layer (mapping sample sets).")
write_tsv(mac_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "carrier_count_audit.tsv"))
```

The MAC ≥ 5 floor is applied at the genotype intersection in module 23
(before outlier exclusion). `r if (all(mac_tab$n_lt5 == 0)) sprintf("This round the floor propagated cleanly: every tested pair in every layer retains ≥ %d minor-allele carriers in EAS and ≥ %d in EUR — no post-hoc carrier filtering is needed.", min(mac_tab$min_carriers[mac_tab$ancestry == "EAS"]), min(mac_tab$min_carriers[mac_tab$ancestry == "EUR"])) else "A fraction of tests retain < 5 carriers in the mapping sample sets (audit table) because the floor predates outlier exclusion and modality-specific sample attrition. No FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited; hit lists should be post-filtered to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source."`

## Stepwise regression: independent signals

`r if (n_groups_stepwise == 0) "No group reached FDR ≤ 5% in any ancestry × modality layer, so no cell produced a stepwise entrant and all independent-signal outputs are empty by design." else sprintf("Of the %d FDR-qualifying groups entering the stepwise scan, **%d carry a conditionally independent secondary signal** (rank ≥ 2); the remainder yielded their primary lead variant alone.", n_groups_stepwise, n_secondary)`

```{r stepwise-table}
if (n_secondary > 0) {
  # group_id exists for grouped/combined runs, absent for expression;
  # fall back to parsing the phenotype id
  gid <- if ("group_id" %in% names(independent)) {
    strip_version(if_else(is.na(independent$group_id),
                          str_split_fixed(independent$phenotype_id, "__", 2)[, 1],
                          independent$group_id))
  } else {
    strip_version(str_split_fixed(independent$phenotype_id, "__", 2)[, 1])
  }
  sec <- independent %>%
    mutate(gene_id = gid, gene_symbol = symd(gene_id)) %>%
    filter(rank >= 2) %>%
    select(ancestry, modality, gene_id, gene_symbol, phenotype_id, variant_id,
           rank, slope, pval_nominal, pval_beta)
  knitr::kable(sec %>% slice_head(n = 100), digits = 3,
               caption = sprintf("Conditionally independent secondary signals (rank ≥ 2; top 100 of %d shown; full table in tables/independent_secondary.tsv).", nrow(sec)))
  write_tsv(sec, file.path(params$table_dir, "independent_secondary.tsv"))
}
```

# eGene characterization

## eGene catalog (FDR ≤ 5%)

```{r egene-catalog}
catalog <- egenes_combined %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = symd(gene_id)) %>%
  select(ancestry, gene_id, gene_symbol, driver_modality,
         driver_phenotype = phenotype_id, variant_id, af, ma_count, slope,
         pval_beta, qval, group_size) %>%
  arrange(ancestry, qval)
write_tsv(catalog, file.path(params$table_dir, "egene_catalog_combined.tsv"))

catalog_mod <- egenes_grouped %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = symd(gene_id)) %>%
  select(ancestry, modality, gene_id, gene_symbol,
         driver_phenotype = phenotype_id, variant_id, af, ma_count, slope,

  arrange(ancestry, modality, qval)
write_tsv(catalog_mod, file.path(params$table_dir, "egene_catalog_by_modality.tsv"))

if (nrow(catalog) > 0) {
  knitr::kable(catalog %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% slice_head(n = 20) %>% ungroup(),
               digits = 3,
               caption = "Combined-layer eGenes (top 20 per ancestry by q-value; full catalog in tables/egene_catalog_combined.tsv).")
}
```

The primary catalog is the **combined cross-modality layer**
(`r n_eg["EAS"]` EAS / `r n_eg["EUR"]` EUR eGenes; full table in
`tables/egene_catalog_combined.tsv`); the per-modality grouped breakdown is
in `tables/egene_catalog_by_modality.tsv`. The driver modality labels which
modality carries the gene's strongest association.

## eGene overlap across modalities and ancestries

```{r egene-overlap, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
# modality overlap of grouped eGenes, per ancestry (UpSet)
for (a in c("EAS", "EUR")) {
  sets <- split(egenes_grouped$gene_id[egenes_grouped$ancestry == a],
                egenes_grouped$modality[egenes_grouped$ancestry == a])
  sets <- sets[lengths(sets) > 0]
  if (length(sets) >= 2) {
    m <- ComplexHeatmap::make_comb_mat(sets)
    m <- m[ComplexHeatmap::comb_size(m) > 0]
    up <- ComplexHeatmap::UpSet(m, set_order = names(sets),
                                comb_order = order(-ComplexHeatmap::comb_size(m)))
    print(up)
    png(file.path(params$fig_dir, sprintf("fig_egene_upset_%s.png", tolower(a))),
        width = 9, height = 5, units = "in", res = 150)
    print(up)
    dev.off()
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("%s: %d modality set(s) with eGenes — UpSet needs ≥ 2; skipped.\n",
                a, length(sets)))
  }
}

# ancestry overlap of combined-layer eGenes
eg_eas <- unique(egenes_combined$gene_id[egenes_combined$ancestry == "EAS"])
eg_eur <- unique(egenes_combined$gene_id[egenes_combined$ancestry == "EUR"])
shared_eg <- intersect(eg_eas, eg_eur)
tested_both <- intersect(combined$gene_id[combined$ancestry == "EAS"],
                         combined$gene_id[combined$ancestry == "EUR"])
overlap_tab <- tibble(
  set = c("EAS only", "shared", "EUR only"),
  n = c(length(setdiff(eg_eas, eg_eur)), length(shared_eg),
        length(setdiff(eg_eur, eg_eas))))
# is the shared fraction more than chance given the two hit rates?
fisher_overlap <- if (length(tested_both) > 0 && (length(eg_eas) + length(eg_eur)) > 0) {
  fisher.test(matrix(c(length(shared_eg),
                       length(eg_eas) - length(shared_eg),
                       length(eg_eur) - length(shared_eg),
                       length(tested_both) - length(eg_eas) - length(eg_eur) + length(shared_eg)),
                     nrow = 2))[c("p.value", "estimate")]
} else NULL
knitr::kable(overlap_tab,
             caption = sprintf("Combined-layer eGene overlap between ancestries (genes tested in both: %s).",
                               format(length(tested_both), big.mark = ",")))
write_tsv(overlap_tab, file.path(params$table_dir, "egene_ancestry_overlap.tsv"))
```

`r if (!is.null(fisher_overlap)) sprintf("Of the %d EAS and %d EUR combined-layer eGenes, **%d are shared** (Fisher exact vs the tested-in-both universe: odds ratio %.2f, p = %s) — shared eGenes are %s than expected under independence.", length(eg_eas), length(eg_eur), length(shared_eg), fisher_overlap$estimate, signif(fisher_overlap$p.value, 2), if (fisher_overlap$estimate > 1) "more frequent" else "less frequent")`

## Functional enrichment (g:Profiler)

```{r enrichment, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
# Over-representation analysis on the combined-layer eGene sets, g:Profiler
# gost with g:SCS correction; background = all genes tested in the
# corresponding stratum (devBrain custom-background convention).
enrich_results <- list()
if (requireNamespace("gprofiler2", quietly = TRUE) && nrow(egenes_combined) > 0) {
  bg_eas <- unique(combined$gene_id[combined$ancestry == "EAS"])
  bg_eur <- unique(combined$gene_id[combined$ancestry == "EUR"])
  enrich_sets <- list(
    "EAS combined eGenes"  = list(genes = eg_eas, bg = bg_eas),
    "EUR combined eGenes"  = list(genes = eg_eur, bg = bg_eur),
    "shared eGenes"        = list(genes = shared_eg, bg = tested_both),
    "EAS-specific eGenes"  = list(genes = setdiff(eg_eas, eg_eur), bg = bg_eas),
    "EUR-specific eGenes"  = list(genes = setdiff(eg_eur, eg_eas), bg = bg_eur)
  )
  for (nm in names(enrich_sets)) {
    es <- enrich_sets[[nm]]
    if (length(es$genes) < 5) {
      message(sprintf("  enrichment: '%s' has %d genes (< 5) — skipped", nm,
                      length(es$genes)))
      next
    }
    res <- tryCatch(
      gprofiler2::gost(es$genes, organism = "hsapiens", ordered_query = FALSE,
                       sources = c("GO:BP", "GO:MF", "GO:CC", "KEGG", "REAC"),
                       custom_bg = es$bg, correction_method = "g_SCS",
                       significant = TRUE),
      error = function(e) { message("  gost failed for '", nm, "': ", e$message); NULL })
    if (is.null(res) || is.null(res$result) || nrow(res$result) == 0) next
    enrich_results[[nm]] <- res$result %>%
      mutate(query_set = nm, n_query = length(es$genes)) %>%
      select(query_set, source, term_id, term_name, p_value, term_size,
             query_size, intersection_size, n_query, any_of("intersection"))
    write_tsv(enrich_results[[nm]],
              file.path(params$table_dir,
                        paste0("enrichment_", make.names(nm), ".tsv")))
  }
} else if (!requireNamespace("gprofiler2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cat("gprofiler2 not installed — enrichment skipped (install.packages('gprofiler2')).\n")
}

if (length(enrich_results) > 0) {
  enrich_all <- bind_rows(enrich_results)
  write_tsv(enrich_all, file.path(params$table_dir, "enrichment_all.tsv"))
  enrich_top <- enrich_all %>% group_by(query_set) %>%
    slice_min(p_value, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(term_label = str_wrap(term_name, 35),
           term_label = forcats::fct_reorder(term_label, -log10(p_value)))
  p_enrich <- ggplot(enrich_top,
                     aes(-log10(p_value), term_label, color = source,
                         size = intersection_size)) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_wrap(~query_set, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = NULL) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "genes", range = c(1.5, 5)) +
    guides(size = guide_legend(title.position = "top"),
           color = guide_legend(title.position = "top")) +
    labs(x = "-log10(g:SCS-adjusted p)", y = NULL) +
    theme_report(base_size = 9) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  print(p_enrich)
  ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_enrichment_dotplot.png"), p_enrich,
         width = 9, height = max(4, 2.6 * length(enrich_results)), dpi = 150)
  knitr::kable(enrich_all %>% group_by(query_set) %>%
                 slice_min(p_value, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
                 select(query_set, source, term_id, term_name, p_value,
                        intersection_size),
               digits = 3,
               caption = "Top 5 enriched terms per eGene set (full tables in tables/enrichment_*.tsv).")
} else {
  cat("No enrichment results (all sets < 5 genes, no significant terms, or g:Profiler unreachable).\n")
}
```

Enrichment is over-representation analysis on the FDR ≤ 5% combined-layer
eGene sets (per ancestry, plus shared and ancestry-specific sets) against
the **tested-gene universe of the same stratum** — not the whole genome —
following the devBrain xQTL convention; g:SCS is g:Profiler's native
multiple-testing correction. Sets with fewer than 5 genes are skipped (ORA
is not meaningful). Full term tables are in `tables/enrichment_*.tsv`.

# Cross-ancestry analysis

Cross-ancestry analysis is comparative only (no pooled p-value combination).

```{r fig-concordance, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.5}
dedup_best <- function(df) df %>% group_by(gene_id) %>%
  slice_min(pval_beta, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
ea <- combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS") %>% dedup_best() %>%
  select(gene_id, pval_beta_a = pval_beta)
eu <- combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EUR") %>% dedup_best() %>%
  select(gene_id, pval_beta_b = pval_beta)
jj <- ea %>% inner_join(eu, by = "gene_id")
rho <- cor(-log10(jj$pval_beta_a), -log10(jj$pval_beta_b), method = "spearman")

lim <- max(c(-log10(jj$pval_beta_a), -log10(jj$pval_beta_b))) * 1.05
p7 <- ggplot(jj, aes(-log10(pval_beta_a), -log10(pval_beta_b))) +
  geom_hex(bins = 60) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", name = "genes") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, lim), ylim = c(0, lim)) +
  annotate("label", x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.8,
           fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, label.size = 0, size = 3.5,
           label = sprintf("Spearman rho = %.3f\n(n = %s genes tested in both)",
                           rho, format(nrow(jj), big.mark = ","))) +
  labs(x = "EAS  -log10(pval_beta), combined layer",
       y = "EUR  -log10(pval_beta), combined layer") +
  theme_report()
print(p7)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_cross_ancestry_concordance.png"), p7,
       width = 7.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r concordance-tables}
conc_combined <- cross_ancestry_concordance(
  combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS") %>% dedup_best(),
  combined %>% filter(ancestry == "EUR") %>% dedup_best()) %>%
  mutate(modality = "combined")
conc_mod <- grouped %>%
  group_by(modality) %>%
  group_modify(~ cross_ancestry_concordance(
    .x %>% filter(ancestry == "EAS") %>% dedup_best(),
    .x %>% filter(ancestry == "EUR") %>% dedup_best())) %>% ungroup()
conc_all <- bind_rows(conc_mod, conc_combined) %>%
  select(modality, n_genes, same_variant, rank_spearman, top100_overlap)
knitr::kable(conc_all, digits = 3,
             caption = "Cross-ancestry concordance per layer: genes tested in both ancestries, same-lead-variant count, Spearman correlation of -log10(pval_beta), and top-100 gene overlap.")
write_tsv(conc_all, file.path(params$table_dir, "cross_ancestry_concordance.tsv"))
```

Rank concordance ranges from `r round(min(conc_all$rank_spearman, na.rm = TRUE), 3)` to
`r round(max(conc_all$rank_spearman, na.rm = TRUE), 3)` across layers
(top-100 overlap at or below chance).
`r if (max(abs(conc_all$rank_spearman), na.rm = TRUE) < 0.1) "The two ancestries' sub-threshold tails do **not** point at the same genes — consistent with the near-misses being noise rather than shared weak signal, and arguing against combining the strata for discovery at these sample sizes." else "Layers with non-trivial rank concordance indicate shared sub-threshold signal; see the table."`

# Transcript-level driver resolution

The combined layer labels each gene-group by its **driver phenotype** (the
phenotype with the best nominal association in the group), and the ungrouped
layer provides per-phenotype lead variants. `r if (n_fdr05 <= 10) "With few FDR-significant associations, this machinery is applied mostly to the top-ranked near-misses for prioritization." else "Applied to the FDR-significant catalog, this resolves which modality and transcript carries each eGene signal."`

## Driver-modality composition of top-ranked genes

```{r fig-driver-modality, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
driver_tab <- combined %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>% mutate(rank_by_q = rank(qval, ties.method = "first")) %>%
  ungroup()
driver_comp <- bind_rows(
  driver_tab %>% filter(rank_by_q <= 50)  %>% count(ancestry, driver_modality) %>% mutate(tier = "top 50"),
  driver_tab %>% filter(rank_by_q <= 200) %>% count(ancestry, driver_modality) %>% mutate(tier = "top 200")
)
p8 <- ggplot(driver_comp, aes(driver_modality, n, fill = driver_modality)) +
  geom_col() + facet_grid(tier ~ ancestry) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = MODALITY_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "genes driven by modality") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
print(p8)
ggsave(file.path(params$fig_dir, "fig_driver_modality.png"), p8,
       width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 150)
write_tsv(driver_comp, file.path(params$table_dir, "driver_modality_composition.tsv"))
```

```{r driver-shares}
shares <- driver_comp %>% filter(tier == "top 50") %>%
  group_by(ancestry) %>% mutate(frac = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()
share_of <- function(anc, mod) {
  x <- shares %>% filter(ancestry == anc, driver_modality == mod)
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return(0)
  round(100 * x$frac)
}
```

```{r driver-top}
top_driver <- shares %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% slice_max(frac, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

`r sprintf("%s drives the largest share of top-ranked genes in %s (%d%% of the top 50)", top_driver$driver_modality[top_driver$ancestry == "EAS"], "EAS", share_of("EAS", as.character(top_driver$driver_modality[top_driver$ancestry == "EAS"])))`;
`r sprintf("%s does so in %s (%d%% of the top 50)", top_driver$driver_modality[top_driver$ancestry == "EUR"], "EUR", share_of("EUR", as.character(top_driver$driver_modality[top_driver$ancestry == "EUR"])))`.
`r if (n_fdr05 <= 10) "With few FDR-significant associations, this is a descriptive property of the sub-threshold tail, not a discovery pattern." else "The same composition computed over FDR-significant eGenes only is in the eGene catalog table above."`

## Within-gene driver breakdown for the top combined genes

For the top 10 combined-layer genes per ancestry, the per-phenotype lead
associations across all modalities (ungrouped layer):

```{r driver-breakdown}

breakdown <- top10 %>%
```

# Biological interpretation

```{r interp-numbers}
mod_leader <- if (nrow(n_eg_mod) > 0) {
  n_eg_mod %>% group_by(ancestry) %>% mutate(total = sum(n)) %>%
    slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
} else NULL
enrich_highlight <- if (exists("enrich_results") && length(enrich_results) > 0) {
  bind_rows(enrich_results) %>% group_by(query_set) %>%
    slice_min(p_value, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
    summarise(hl = paste(sprintf("%s — %s (%s, g:SCS p = %s)", query_set,
                                 term_name, source, signif(p_value, 2)),
                         collapse = "; ")) %>% pull(hl)
} else NA_character_
```

**The discovery landscape this round: `r n_fdr05` FDR ≤ 5% associations —
`r n_eg["EAS"]` EAS and `r n_eg["EUR"]` EUR eGenes in the primary
combined-layer catalog** (n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`/`r n_samp["EUR"]`, MAF ≥
0.01 + MAC ≥ 5, genome-wide permutation calibration). Strongest per
ancestry:
`r paste(sprintf("%s: %s", top_by_anc$ancestry, apply(top_by_anc, 1, function(r) sprintf("%s (%s, %s layer, q = %s, r² ≈ %.2f)", symd(r[["gene_id"]]), r[["modality"]], r[["layer"]], signif(as.numeric(r[["qval"]]), 2), approx_r2(as.numeric(r[["slope"]]), as.numeric(r[["af"]]))))), collapse = "; ")`.
`r if (!is.null(hit_r2)) sprintf("Hit effect sizes (r² %.2f–%.2f) sit in the class the power floor permits.", hit_r2[1], hit_r2[2])`
All hits should be treated as candidates: visual QC of phenotype levels by
genotype and replication in larger placental cohorts come before functional
claims.

Three **characterization** observations:

1. **Modality composition.** `r if (!is.null(mod_leader)) paste(sprintf("%s leads the %s grouped-eGene breakdown (%d of %d)", mod_leader$modality, mod_leader$ancestry, mod_leader$n, mod_leader$total), collapse = "; ") else "No grouped-layer eGenes this round."`
   PANTRY's central finding was that non-expression modalities carry the
   largest share of regulatory signal; the driver-modality composition of
   the catalog (above) tests whether that ordering holds in placenta.
2. **Ancestry sharing.** `r if (!is.null(fisher_overlap)) sprintf("%d of %d EAS and %d EUR combined-layer eGenes are shared (Fisher OR %.2f, p = %s vs the tested-in-both universe).", length(shared_eg), length(eg_eas), length(eg_eur), fisher_overlap$estimate, signif(fisher_overlap$p.value, 2)) else "Ancestry overlap was not computed (empty eGene set)."`
   Shared eGenes are the cross-ancestry replication signal; specific sets
   are candidates for ancestry-biased regulation.
3. **Functional enrichment.** `r if (!is.na(enrich_highlight)) paste0("Top g:Profiler term per set: ", enrich_highlight, ". Full tables in tables/enrichment_*.tsv.") else "No significant enrichment terms (or sets too small for ORA) — see the enrichment section."`

Sub-threshold top-ranked genes (tables above) remain prioritization hints
only`r if (any(mac_tab$n_lt5 > 0)) " — and the flagged low-carrier rows should be discounted outright" else ""`.

# Limitations and next steps

1. **Power.** n ≈ `r n_samp["EAS"]`/`r n_samp["EUR"]` with a ~12k-gene
   testing burden detects only r² ≳ 0.10 (EAS) / 0.19 (EUR) effects.
   Doubling n would roughly halve the detectable r²; matching PANTRY's
   n = 445 would bring the floor to ≈ 0.06. Adding the remaining cohorts and
   the AFR/AMR/SAS strata is the highest-value next step.
2. **Carrier-count propagation.** `r if (all(mac_tab$n_lt5 == 0)) "Resolved this round: the MAC ≥ 5 floor propagated cleanly to every mapping output (audit table above)." else "The MAC ≥ 5 floor predates outlier exclusion, so low-carrier tests persist in some mapping outputs (audit table above). No reported result depends on them; hit lists should post-filter to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source."`
3. **Ancestry asymmetry.** EUR tests more phenotypes than EAS in every
   modality (ancestry-specific filtering), so cross-ancestry comparisons are
   restricted to genes tested in both.
4. **No pooled cross-ancestry inference** was performed. If combined
   discovery is wanted later, Fisher/Stouffer or an inverse-variance slope
   meta-analysis are the clean options.
5. **Stepwise secondary signals**: `r if (n_secondary == 0) "none called in any layer this round." else sprintf("%d groups carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (table above).", n_secondary)`
6. **Fine-mapping and colocalization are out of scope this round.** The
   natural follow-ups on the FDR-significant catalog are SuSiE fine-mapping
   per eGene locus, GWAS colocalization (coloc/eCAVIAR) against placental
   and pregnancy-outcome GWAS, and locus-zoom visual QC of each hit
   (nominal-scan extraction + LD from the ancestry-matched genotype panel).
7. **Replication path**: the FDR-significant hits are the priorities for
   lookup in larger placental resources or a future meta-analysis; visual QC
   of phenotype levels by genotype is the immediate sanity check for each.

# Reproducibility

- Results: tensorQTL cis mapping (grouped / ungrouped / combined / stepwise),
  MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5 at the genotype intersection, ±1 Mb window, **Storey
  q-values** on pval_beta via the R `qvalue` package (singularity-R bridge).
  Covariates: as described (first-5 PCs + HCP_1–k\* + sex/GA/cell types;
  maternal fraction excluded before correlation pruning; no cap). Genotype
  PCs: cohort-only plink2 PCA on LD-pruned variants.
- Pipeline scripts: this repository (`05_qtl_mapping/`, scripts 19–30 +
  `compute_qvalues.R`; genotype pooling in `01_genotype_imputation/`).
- Report code: `report_placenta_xqtl.Rmd` + `xqtl_report_functions.R`;
  figures in `figures/`, tables in `tables/`.
- Gene symbols: `gene_map.tsv` regenerated in full from the normalized GTF
  (config `normalized_gtf`) by `make_report_archive.sh` at archive time —
  covers every tested gene, version-stripped IDs.
